title: Shared browser inspection
summary: Browser inspection MUST run as tabs in the one shared Chrome for Testing instance, which never borrows the operator's personal browser identity, and MUST leave no page or host setting behind.
instructions: Browser inspection and Visual QA MUST use the `chrome-devtools` MCP server. Playwright MCP is an explicit fallback only when chrome-devtools is unavailable, and the fallback MUST be disclosed in case evidence.

All agents MUST share one long-lived headless Chrome for Testing instance with a dedicated user-data-dir; no browser window exists. Every `chrome-devtools` MCP server MUST attach to it with `--browserUrl=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` and nothing else: `--isolated`, `--executablePath`, and `--headless` MUST NOT appear on the server. Each agent MUST open its own tab with `new_page` (a unique `isolatedContext` name keeps storage separate), MUST close it with `close_page`, and MUST NOT launch a browser of its own. Agents MUST NOT bring any browser window to the foreground or rely on a visible window; a visible browser window on the operator's desktop is a defect to report. Agents MUST NOT attach to an operator's personal browser or drive MCP automation through the personal `com.google.Chrome` identity.

The shared instance MUST be a Chrome for Testing bundle. `pan doctor` reports whether that bundle is present and whether the server attaches over `--browserUrl`; when either is absent, agents MUST report the readiness gap rather than fall back to an installed personal browser.
Agents MUST close every page they open with `close_page` when inspection finishes, including on failure.
Agents MUST NOT change macOS Launch Services, the default browser, or Chrome preferences as remediation, and MUST NOT kill or quit all MCP Chrome processes as the primary remediation.

Enforcement of the preceding prohibition is mechanical, not advisory: the operator's `beforeShellExecution` hook `~/.cursor/hooks/deny-browser-env-write.py` denies shell commands that rebind the `http`/`https` handlers, write the Launch Services handler database, mutate the personal Chrome preference domain or profile tree, or kill a browser by name. Read-only diagnosis stays available. A genuine repair MUST be authorised by the operator, who prefixes the single command with `ALLOW_BROWSER_ENV_WRITE=1`; an agent MUST NOT set that variable for itself, and MUST report the block instead.
Case evidence MUST record every Chrome DevTools MCP action, DOM observation, `isolatedContext` confirmation, and every `close_page` action.

When neither chrome-devtools nor the Playwright fallback is available, a stage that owes a browser verdict MUST report the case as environment-blocked. It MUST NOT convert the gap into a product pass or fail, and MUST NOT substitute a screenshot or capture fallback for a required browser verdict.
Design exploration and iteration MAY use a disclosed non-browser capture fallback, because it produces craft feedback rather than a verdict.
When one stage already owns browser inspection for a surface, another stage MUST NOT duplicate it; it MUST record its own verification and reference the existing evidence.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you open a browser page or record a browser verdict.
